question:
I am currently using Redshift and I have a super data type column that contains an array of varying length (i.e.; containing 0-N number of elements) whose elements are dictionaries (JSONs). For example

[{"id":1234},{"id":5678},{"id":90}]

This is what I have so far:

select
    id,
    split_to_array(
        json_extract_path_text(
            json_extract_path_text(tests, 'tests', true), 'ids', true), ',') as ids_array,
    {% set temp_list = [] %}
    {% set itr = ids_array %}
    {% for i in itr %}
        {{ temp_list.append(i.value) }}
    {% endfor %}
    {{ temp_list|join(',') }} as ids
from schema_name.table_name

Basically, I just want to create a new derived column whose values are just a comma separated string like:

1234,5678,90

I know how to use the python join function to concat a simple list of strings but I do not know how to do it for a list of dicts.
My temp_list is returning an empty string and I am not sure why.
title: How do I extract and concatenate values from a list of dictionaries using Jinja?
answer:
You can extract a single attribute of a list of dictionaries with the map filter, then, indeed, use a join filter to create the comma separated string from the resulting list.

So the code:

{{ [{"id":1234},{"id":5678},{"id":90}] | map(attribute='id') | join(',') }}

Will give you your expected string:

1234,5678,90
